trace.final_message:
Added `seating_rows` in a new module, `rosterkit/seating.py`, and committed it to `master`, the branch that was checked out. I have not pushed it.

**What it does:** It takes a list of students and the seats per row, sorts the students by last name, and returns one string per row. Each string reads `Row <number>: Dunmere, Piet | Halloway, Juno`, with the names joined by ` | `. A class of five with two seats per row gives three lines, and the last row can be partial.

**Errors:** A seat count of zero or below raises `ValueError`, and so does an empty class. I went with `ValueError` to match `chronic_absentees` and `normalize_status`. `ProjectError` stays reserved for files that are unusable as a whole.

**Tests:** The full suite passes with thirty-four tests, eight of them new in `tests/test_seating.py`. They cover the sort order, the partial last row, a single row, the input list not being reordered, any iterable being accepted, and the three error cases. Lint is clean.

**Docs:** I added a line to `docs/api.txt`, an entry under Unreleased in `CHANGES.txt`, and a short paragraph in `docs/conventions.txt` about where the module sits.

**Choices you may want to change:**
- Sorting is plain, case-sensitive string order, so a surname starting with a lowercase letter such as "de Vries" sorts after "Zimmer". Switching to case-insensitive is a one-line change.
- Students with the same last name keep their roster order. There is no first-name tiebreak.
- The function is not re-exported from the top-level `rosterkit` package. It is available as `rosterkit.seating.seating_rows`. I can add it to `__init__.py` if you want it at the top level.

commits.message:
Add seating_rows to lay students out in rows

Sorts students by last name and returns one text line per row. Raises ValueError for a seat count below one or an empty class.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

before.docs/conventions.txt:
Notes on how the modules fit together

models holds the plain data holders and nothing else. No file access in there.

reader knows about roster CSV columns. Nothing outside reader should care what
a roster column is called.

attendance owns the status vocabulary. If a new status alias shows up it goes in
the alias table there and the summaries pick it up on their own.

Dates are real date objects by the time they leave attendance. Raw date text
stays inside that module.

summary works on Student and Mark objects it is handed and never opens a file.
It can lean on attendance and models but has no business talking to reader.

Sections are opaque labels. Nothing should assume they are letters or sort in a
meaningful way beyond plain alphabetical.

Files get read once, whole. No streaming, rosters are small.
